name: Research Labs

orgs.name: Allen Institute for AI
orgs.note: Ai2 (the Allen Institute for AI) describes itself as a non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by Paul G. Allen; source URL verified 2026-08-14

blurb:
This section profiles the frontier and industrial research labs, recording the parent organisation, leadership, funding model and published work for each. It separates organisations that publish research from product companies that do not, so a lab inside a large public company appears here rather than only under its parent's ticker.

Read it today as a placeholder rather than a roster. Membership is not set by a feed: an organisation appears only after someone classifies it by hand as a research lab in the company register. Coverage therefore tracks editorial capacity, not the state of the field, and an organisation can sit in the database for months and still be missing here simply because nobody has tagged it.

The section currently holds one entry, Ai2, the Allen Institute for AI, a non-profit research institute founded in 2014 by Paul G. Allen and verified against its own about page. That is one lab out of 269 organisations in the register. The neighbouring classifications are nearly as thin: two university labs, two government labs, two open-source foundations and two non-profits, against 40 public companies and 39 startups, with 181 organisations carrying no classification at all.

No frontier lab appears here yet. OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral AI and Cohere are all in the register but tagged as startups, and Meta and Microsoft as public companies, so their absence reflects how they are tagged rather than any judgement about their research. Two things would make this section worth reading: classifying the labs already in the register, and capturing the funding model and leadership detail the section promises, neither of which is recorded even for the single entry it has.

reading.body:
Research labs are organizational units conducting frontier or industrial AI work, though this data covers only one entity and thus cannot characterize the category's scale or diversity.

The Allen Institute for AI stands as a non-profit model for AI research, distinct from the venture-backed and corporate labs that dominate frontier development. Its founding in 2014 by a technology billionaire represents one path to sustained research capacity outside traditional academic and industry structures. The institute's self-description emphasizes independence, though the data does not specify its funding sources beyond the founding relationship, its annual operating budget, or whether it operates specialized computing facilities.

This entry documents organizational form rather than capabilities, infrastructure, or output. It does not reveal how research labs relate to the compute, buildings, or power systems that constrain AI scaling. Whether non-profit labs operate their own data centers, purchase capacity from cloud providers, or depend on university infrastructure remains outside the scope here. The single example also cannot show whether non-profit research institutions represent a growing or shrinking share of frontier AI work.
